one_liner: Vitis HLS FPGA design for fixed-width arbitrary-precision floating-point matrix multiply, about 10x a 36-core MPFR node (FCCM'22).
what_it_does: APFP is a hardware design for Xilinx XRT FPGAs (built for an Alveo U250) that implements a fully pipelined multi-hundred-bit floating-point multiplier and adder and exposes them only through a tiled matrix-multiplication kernel (plus a multiply microbenchmark kernel). The host side is a small C++ class (interface/Apfp.h): allocate DeviceMatrix buffers, copy GMP mpf_t arrays to the card, call Apfp::MatrixMultiplication, copy back. It is not a general MPFR replacement: there are no other operations, no scalar API, and a BLAS-compatibility layer exists only as unmerged PR #7.
how_it_is_fast: The mantissa multiplier is a compile-time recursive Karatsuba decomposition (device/Karatsuba.cpp) that bottoms out at APFP_MULT_BASE_BITS (default 36) in DSP multipliers, and wide additions are split into manually pipelined stages above APFP_ADD_BASE_BITS, so the whole multiply-accumulate is fully pipelined at one MAC per cycle per compute unit. The GEMM is tiled with the communication-avoiding scheme from the authors' FPGA'20 paper (default 32x32 tiles in on-chip memory) so DRAM bandwidth does not limit it, and APFP_COMPUTE_UNITS replicates the kernel across the U250's DDR banks and SLRs.
when_to_use: Large dense matrix multiplications at 448-bit or 960-bit mantissa precision (APFP_BITS 512 or 1024) that dominate a run, such as the semidefinite-programming solvers the paper targets.
You already have an Alveo U250 (or another XRT platform you are willing to port the DDR mapping to) and a Vitis HLS toolchain.
Throughput matters more than latency: matrices large enough to fill 32x32 tiles and amortize host-to-card transfers.
Research on FPGA arithmetic: the Karatsuba and pipelined-adder templates are a compact reference for wide-integer datapaths in HLS.
when_not_to_use: Anything other than matrix multiply: no division, square root, transcendental functions or element-wise kernels, and the host interface's transpose is unimplemented; use MPFR, or a GPU MPFR backend for batched scalars.

When you need MPFR's rounding modes or special values: only round-toward-zero (MPFR_RNDZ) is supported, the adder flushes underflow to zero, and PackedFloat asks 'Should we just assume nan/inf can't appear?'.
Precision chosen at run time or not a multiple of 512 bits: APFP_BITS is fixed at build time and CMake rejects values not aligned to 512.
Products you need to ship or redistribute: the repository has no license file, and it has been inactive since 2022-05-17.
Machines without an FPGA, or teams without days for hardware builds: 'make hw' runs a full Vitis synthesis and place-and-route.

integration.form: FPGA bitstream (.xclbin) built with Vitis, driven from your own host code; the ApfpHostlib shared library is unfinished (see gotchas)
integration.dependencies: Xilinx Vitis HLS and XRT, GMP, MPFR, Threads, hlslib (git submodule)
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (-std=c++17 in CMakeLists.txt), CMake 3.0+, Vitis version not stated
integration.platforms: Xilinx XRT FPGAs; default platform xilinx_u250_gen3x16_xdma_3_1_202020_1, DDR bank mapping hard-coded for the U250; CPU-only simulation build for testing

gotchas: The installable host library (interface/Apfp.cpp) looks unfinished: DeviceMatrix::TransferToHost copies the raw device format (kBytes per number, 128 bytes at the default 1024 bits) straight into the caller's mpf_t array, which overruns a buffer of 24-byte mpf_t structs and produces no valid GMP values, and its size check (>=) rejects an exactly sized buffer. The kernel path is an empty string, ApfpHostlib is compiled with HLSLIB_SIMULATE_OPENCL, and Transpose/TransposeInPlace just throw. The benchmark programs in host/ do not use this interface.
APFP_BITS counts the whole number: 64 bits go to the packed sign and exponent, so 512-bit numbers have a 448-bit mantissa and 1024-bit numbers a 960-bit mantissa.

Only MPFR_RNDZ is supported (DeviceTypes.h: 'the only MPFR rounding mode supported'); the test programs check bit-exact equality against an MPFR RNDZ reference, so results match MPFR only under round-toward-zero.

Tile sizes, compute units, frequency and the DDR bank mapping (hard-coded for the U250) must be configured for the target card; the README says the accelerator 'should always be configured to match the target system'.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick APFP over MPLAPACK's quad-double or CUDA backends, MultiFloats.jl or DoubleFloats.jl when you need far more than ~200 bits of mantissa in GEMM and own an Alveo U250; pick gnu-mpfr-cgbn or MPLAPACK instead if you have a GPU or need operations other than matrix multiply.
verified_claims_summary: The README repeats the FCCM'22 result: 2.0 GMAC/s of 512-bit matrix-matrix multiplication on an Alveo U250, about ten times a dual-socket 36-core Xeon node running MPFR (375 CPU cores' worth); search summaries of the paper abstract add 9.8x at 4.8 GOp/s for 512-bit and 5.3x at 1.2 GOp/s for 1024-bit multiplication. The repo's host programs (host/Microbenchmark.cpp, host/TestMatrixMultiplication.cpp) do time and print an MPFR reference, but it is a single-threaded triple loop of mpfr_mul and mpfr_add used for bit-exact verification, not the 36-core baseline; the CPU model, compiler, flags and MPFR version of the paper's baseline are not in the repo.
status_note: Abandoned research artifact (last commit 2022-05-17, three PRs open since early 2022) with no license file, so treat it as reference code for study, not something to vendor.
